events.blurb: William of Normandy defeats Harold at Hastings and is crowned king of England. The Conquest ties England to the continent, replaces its aristocracy with Normans, and reshapes its language.
events.label: Norman Conquest, 1066

events.blurb: Crusaders storm Jerusalem after a three-year march, massacring its Muslim and Jewish inhabitants and founding the Kingdom of Jerusalem. The First Crusade's success hardens the religious frontier for centuries.
events.label: Crusaders take Jerusalem, 1099

events.blurb: King John seals Magna Carta at Runnymede, conceding that the king is subject to law. Its clauses on counsel and judgment become the foundation text of limited monarchy.
events.label: Magna Carta, 1215

events.blurb: Mongol armies crush the Poles at Legnica and the Hungarians at Mohi within days of each other, then withdraw on the death of the Great Khan. Europe escapes conquest by succession politics in Karakorum.
events.label: Mongols invade Europe, 1241

events.blurb: Plague reaches Europe from the Black Sea, killing roughly a third of the continent in four years. The labor shortage that follows ends serfdom in the west and empties whole villages.
events.label: Black Death, 1347

events.blurb: Mehmed II takes Constantinople after a fifty-three-day siege, ending the Byzantine Empire after eleven centuries. Greek scholars flee west with their manuscripts, feeding the Renaissance.
events.label: Fall of Constantinople, 1453

events.blurb: Columbus lands in the Bahamas, believing he has reached Asia. The voyage joins two worlds that had not touched for ten thousand years, and begins the European colonization of the Americas.
events.label: Columbus reaches the Americas, 1492

events.blurb: Martin Luther posts his 95 Theses at Wittenberg, challenging indulgences and, within years, the papacy itself. The Reformation splits western Christendom for good.
events.label: Luther's 95 Theses, 1517

events.blurb: The surviving ship of Magellan's expedition returns to Spain, completing the first circumnavigation of the globe. The voyage proves the world is round, larger than believed, and mostly ocean.
events.label: First circumnavigation, 1522

events.blurb: Copernicus publishes De revolutionibus on his deathbed, moving the Earth from the center of the universe. The book waits seventy years for its revolution to begin.
events.label: Copernicus publishes, 1543

events.blurb: The Spanish Armada, sent to invade England and restore Catholicism, is scattered by storms and English fireships around Gravelines. Spain's naval supremacy is broken, and England's sea power begins.
events.label: Spanish Armada defeated, 1588

events.blurb: English settlers found Jamestown in Virginia, the first permanent English colony in the Americas. It survives starvation, war with the Powhatan, and its own investors' impatience.
events.label: Jamestown founded, 1607

events.blurb: The Peace of Westphalia ends the Thirty Years' War, the most destructive conflict Europe had known. It establishes the sovereign state as the basic unit of international order.
events.label: Peace of Westphalia, 1648

events.blurb: Parliament invites William and Mary to take the English throne, deposing James II without a battle. The Glorious Revolution settles parliamentary supremacy and a Bill of Rights.
events.label: Glorious Revolution, 1688

events.blurb: Frederick of Prussia invades Silesia, opening the Seven Years' War, fought in Europe, North America, India, and at sea. It is the first war waged on a genuinely global scale.
events.label: Seven Years' War begins, 1756

events.blurb: The American colonies declare independence from Britain, and with French help win it. The republic they found becomes the model and the rival of the European order.
events.label: American Independence, 1776

events.blurb: Parisians storm the Bastille, and the National Assembly proclaims the rights of man. The Revolution overturns the old order in France and then, through war, across Europe.
events.label: French Revolution, 1789

events.blurb: Wellington and Blücher defeat Napoleon at Waterloo, ending twenty-three years of French revolutionary and imperial war. The victors' settlement at Vienna holds the peace for nearly a century.
events.label: Waterloo, 1815

events.blurb: Revolution sweeps Europe from Paris to Vienna to Berlin, toppling kings and demanding constitutions. Almost every revolt fails within a year, but the old order never fully recovers.
events.label: Revolutions of 1848

events.blurb: The Kingdom of Italy is proclaimed under Victor Emmanuel II, uniting most of the peninsula after Garibaldi's Thousand conquered the south. The Risorgimento remakes the map of Europe.
events.label: Italy united, 1861

events.blurb: Austria's ultimatum to Serbia, after the assassination at Sarajevo, draws the alliance system into the First World War. Four empires collapse before it ends.
events.label: First World War begins, 1914

events.blurb: The Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd, and within five years a communist state rules a sixth of the Earth's land. The Russian Revolution defines the twentieth century's politics.
events.label: Russian Revolution, 1917

events.blurb: Germany invades Poland, and Britain and France declare war. The Second World War kills more people than any conflict in history and ends with the atomic bomb and a divided Europe.
events.label: Second World War begins, 1939

events.blurb: The war ends with the United Nations founded at San Francisco, an attempt to give the world what the League of Nations could not: a working peace.
events.label: United Nations founded, 1945

events.blurb: Six European states sign the Treaty of Rome, founding the European Economic Community. The coal-and-steel experiment grows into the European Union.
events.label: Treaty of Rome, 1957

events.blurb: Apollo 11 lands two men on the Moon, watched by a fifth of humanity. The space race's peak becomes the century's most shared moment.
events.label: Moon landing, 1969

events.blurb: The Berlin Wall falls as East Germans cross into the West, and the Cold War ends without a shot. Germany reunites within a year, and the Soviet Union dissolves within two.
events.label: Berlin Wall falls, 1989

events.blurb: Hijacked airliners destroy the World Trade Center and damage the Pentagon, killing nearly three thousand people. The attacks launch two decades of war in Afghanistan and Iraq.
events.label: September 11 attacks, 2001

events.blurb: The World Health Organization declares COVID-19 a pandemic. Within months the virus has reached every continent, killed millions, and shut down the world's economies and borders.
events.label: COVID-19 pandemic, 2020
